about: bank 0 $7800-$7FFF and $A000-$A7FF: aiming the ship, player movement for the four waves, rheostat tics and residue, the tic sine table, then the display list start/end routines and the view routine of every game phase

B0:784D.name: aim_home_yaw
B0:784D.desc: sets the yaw rate of turn (RHS_RAT of RHEOY) so that the ship turns back to head along -x, the heading every wave starts with. It is the yaw half of AIMDTH with the front/back test on minus the ship's A,X and without the COMB (a NOP is in its place). Called by L778C while the probot wave ends, followed by S1RHYW

B0:78C7.name: S1MV
B0:78C7.desc: the Star Wars routine SMVSP1/S1MV, instruction for instruction (the matcher missed it): star field viewer x = frame counter shifted left 7, so the stars stream past. It is the whole player movement of the TIE fighter wave, called after RESIDU

B0:7963.name: smv_probot
B0:7963.desc: player movement of the probot wave (wave 1). Sets the x and y speed from the ship's forward axis (unit vector A,X and B,X, each / 32), adds a side slip along the ship's side axis (A,Y and B,Y) in proportion to the sight's x deflection, then falls into L79C9 to move the ship. SMVG0B is the same code for the walker wave

B0:79C9.name: smv_probot_adv
B0:79C9.desc: moves the ship by its x and y speed (both the ship block and the download block), then sets the z speed from the sight's y deflection times the horizontal speed (|x speed| + |y speed|) and moves the height, kept between $0200 and $0C00. Changed from Star Wars S1MVGD. Entered by falling through from L7963

B0:7A95.name: smv_walker_adv
B0:7A95.desc: the same as L79C9 for the walker wave, entered by falling through from SMVG9B: moves the ship in x and y, sets the z speed from the sight's y deflection and the horizontal speed, and keeps the height between $0200 and $1C00

B0:7AFB.name: smv_descend
B0:7AFB.desc: player movement while the walker wave ends (phase $24): x and y speed straight from the ship's forward axis / 32 with no steering from the sight, then L7B0D moves the ship and brings it down

B0:7B04.name: smv_descend_vy
B0:7B04.desc: part of L7AFB, reached by falling through: y speed = forward axis y (unit vector B,X) / 32

B0:7B0D.name: smv_descend_adv
B0:7B0D.desc: part of L7AFB, reached by falling through: moves the ship by its x and y speed (ship block and download block), sets the z speed to -$0400 and lowers the height by it each frame down to the floor of $0200

B0:7B5C.name: s1_roll_add
B0:7B5C.desc: adds A (signed tics) to the roll residue and lets RHRSDU take whole magic steps out of it, rolling the ship (S1RL) when it gives one. Called every frame with A = 8 in the TIE fighter wave and A = -12 in the asteroid wave, which keeps the ship rolling slowly

B0:7B8B.name: RHTRIG
B0:7B8B.desc: the Star Wars routine RHTRIG (the matcher missed it because ESB assembles the block offsets as 8-bit): X points to a rheostat block. Half the size of its rate of turn RHS_RAT is added, with the rate's sign, to its tic residue RHS_RSD, held at $7F or $81 on overflow

B0:7BB1.name: RHRSDU
B0:7BB1.desc: the Star Wars routine RHRSDU (missed for the same 8-bit offsets): X points to a rheostat block. If the size of its residue is at least 78 tics it takes 78 off and sets M_SIN/M_COS for the 4.99 degree magic angle, else if at least 14 it takes 14 off and sets them for the .895 degree angle, with the sine signed like the residue. Returns Z clear when the caller has to rotate, Z set when there is nothing to do

B0:7C07.name: RESIDU
B0:7C07.desc: the Star Wars routine RESIDU (missed because the residue addresses are direct page here): turns the downloaded unit vectors (BIC MS_U1BC) by what is left in the pitch, yaw and roll residues, each through RESCNV and the matrix processor's pitch, yaw or roll program. The ship's own vectors only turn in magic steps and this makes the view turn smoothly

B0:7C7E.name: bank_roll_u1
B0:7C7E.desc: rolls the downloaded unit vectors (BIC 5) by GD_ACT, the amount S1TWGD has banked the ground flyer, which in ESB is not rolled into the ship's own vectors. Bits 6-11 of |GD_ACT| times 3 make an angle in 256ths of a turn for the table roll at LB4B2, the low 6 bits are tics looked up in the tic table for a second roll with MS_ROLL, both signed like GD_ACT. Called by the view routines of the probot and walker waves after RESIDU

B0:A331.name: ivgen1_wait
B0:A331.desc: Star Wars IVGEN1/IVGEN, changed: starts a display list. Waits until the IRQ has handed over a buffer (VGSYNC plus), points Y to its first instruction at offset $3A and stores the JSRL to VGINIT, then calls bank 1 KD8AC through L60BA, which resets the object draw position and adds a JSRL $32AC. Every view routine begins with it

B0:A342.name: load_vg_set
B0:A342.desc: Star Wars DOWNVG, changed to choose between four sets: copies display list set B (0-3, pointers at LB974) from program ROM to the pseudo vector ROM at $2800-$2FFF. When B is not the set already loaded ($48CD) it first sends an empty display list and waits for the next buffer, so that nothing in the pseudo ROM is being drawn while it changes. The phase init routines call it with 0 for the attract and select screens, 1 for the probot and walker waves and 2 for the TIE fighter and asteroid waves, VGDONE calls it to reload the current set after a buffer overrun

B0:A448.name: vew_walker
B0:A448.desc: view of the walker wave (phases $20 and $22). As IPARM, which views the probot wave, with the walker views (page 1 P1_88FD, page 0 P0_891A, page 0 P0_969D) and their lazar collision test (page 3 P3_97CB) in place of the probot ones

B0:A48A.name: vew_walker_end
B0:A48A.desc: view of the end of the walker wave (phase $24, 40 frames): score, shields, sight, ground stars, lazars and explosions without the walkers, then the picture at the start of the pseudo ROM set growing from small to full size 120 below the centre, with the message 'REBEL HIDEOUT'

B0:A515.name: vew_tie
B0:A515.desc: view of the TIE fighter wave (phases $26 and $28): residue, score, shields, VWDTHB, sight, stars, explosions, lazars, the alien ships (SNVW), guns, collisions and glow. It ends with a line that alternates every 128 frames between 'SHOOT nn TIE FIGHTERS FOR BONUS', with the count $4C53 drawn into the gap ('5,000 POINTS AND JEDI LETTER AWARDED' once the count is 0), and 'SHOOT ENEMY SHOTS TO SAVE YOUR SHIELDS'

B0:A599.name: vew_tie_end
B0:A599.desc: view of the end of the TIE fighter wave (phase $2A): as LA515 without the message line and with LA8F8 in place of VWDTHB, which draws the same far object at its saved screen position and moves it 16 to the left each frame

B0:A5CF.name: vew_tie_die
B0:A5CF.desc: view for PHES0D, the player dying in the TIE fighter wave: residue, score, shields, stars, explosions, alien ships, guns, the growing GAME OVER message and glow, no sight and no lazars. The ESB form of Star Wars VEWS0D

B0:A5F9.name: vew_asteroid
B0:A5F9.desc: view of the asteroid wave (phase $2C): residue, score, shields, sight, stars, explosions, lazars, the asteroids (page 2 P2_9983), guns, collisions, LA843 (an object that appears near the end of the wave) and a line that alternates every 128 frames between 'SURVIVE TO EARN NEXT JEDI LETTER' and 'AVOID COLLISIONS WITH ASTEROIDS'

B0:A63E.name: vew_asteroid_end
B0:A63E.desc: view of the end of the asteroid wave (phase $2E, 70 frames): residue, score, shields, stars, explosions, the message '5,000 POINTS AND JEDI LETTER AWARDED', the object of LA881 and the shrinking picture of LA763

B0:A66A.name: vew_asteroid_die
B0:A66A.desc: view for phase $3C (entered through L73AA), the player dying in the asteroid wave: residue, score, shields, stars, explosions, the asteroids, guns, the growing GAME OVER message and glow

B0:A697.name: vew_manual
B0:A697.desc: view of the rebel training manual pages of the attract mode (phase after PHINXT): residue, score, shields, guns and LB20A, which shows 'REBEL TRAINING MANUAL SECTION' with its numbers and the objects of the wave being explained

B0:A6B2.name: vew_wave_bonus
B0:A6B2.desc: view of the bonus screen after the asteroid wave (phase $32): score, shields and the picture at the start of the pseudo ROM set. For the first 64 frames it shows 'WAVE COMPLETED: 2,500 POINTS'. For the next 64, if the start bonus is still due ($4C62), it shows the bonus for the starting difficulty: none for easy, 100,000 for moderate, 250,000 for hard, or from difficulty 3 up 'BONUS AWARDED FOR CONTINUED PLAY' with the 8-digit amount at $4BEF

B0:A763.name: vw_shrink_pic
B0:A763.desc: draws a picture made of seven vector ROM pieces ($34A2 to $3646), each with its own move, scale and JSRL. The scale comes from the low byte of the phase timer, 4 steps a frame up to $F8, so the picture starts full size 600 below the centre and shrinks towards the point 600 right and 200 above it. Called by LA63E at the end of the asteroid wave. Preserves X and U

4801.name: tmp_scal
4801.desc: temp of LA763 (word): the scale instruction for the pieces of the shrinking picture. The address is the shared temp of many routines

486C.name: rheop_rate
486C.desc: RHS_RAT of the pitch block RHEOP: pitch rate of turn, set by AIM and AIMDTH and turned into tics by RHTRIG

486D.name: rheop_rsd
486D.desc: RHS_RSD of the pitch block RHEOP: pitch tics still to be turned. RHRSDU takes whole magic steps from it, RESIDU turns the view by the rest

486F.name: RHEOR
486F.desc: ROLL BLOCK (Atari's name, $4870 in Star Wars): it lies over the yaw block and only its RHS_RSD byte at $4877 is used

4875.name: rheoy_rate
4875.desc: RHS_RAT of the yaw block RHEOY: yaw rate of turn, set by AIM, AIMDTH and L784D and turned into tics by RHTRIG

4876.name: rheoy_rsd
4876.desc: RHS_RSD of the yaw block RHEOY: yaw tics still to be turned

4877.name: rheor_rsd
4877.desc: RHS_RSD of the roll block RHEOR: roll tics still to be turned. L7B5C adds the steady roll of the TIE fighter and asteroid waves to it

48CD.name: vg_set
48CD.desc: number (0-3) of the display list set that LA342 last copied to the pseudo vector ROM at $2800. The self test uses the same byte as the low byte of SWNEW

4BEF.name: cont_bonus
4BEF.desc: 8 BCD digits (4 bytes): the bonus for continued play, shown on the select screen and by LA6B2 and added to the score by LB5D4. At the end of a game it is set from the score saved when the last set of waves was completed

4BFB.name: bcd_lo
4BFB.desc: BCD+2: the low two digits of BINBCD's result

4C53.name: bonus_left
4C53.desc: number of targets still to shoot in the current wave for its bonus and Jedi letter: loaded from the wave's quota when the wave starts, counted down as they are hit, shown in the wave status line and in the TIE fighter wave's message

4C62.name: bonus_due
4C62.desc: 1 from the start of a game until its first wave bonus screen has been shown: LA6B2 then shows the start bonus and phase $32 awards it (LB5D4) and clears the flag

4CAC.name: ph_tim_lo
4CAC.desc: PH_TIM+1: low byte of the phase timer

5032.name: u1_by
5032.desc: MS_BY+M_U1: unit vector B,Y of the ship 1 download block, word (the ship's side axis, y part)

5034.name: u1_bz
5034.desc: MS_BZ+M_U1: unit vector B,Z of the ship 1 download block, word (the ship's up axis, y part)

503A.name: u1_cy
503A.desc: MS_CY+M_U1: unit vector C,Y of the ship 1 download block, word (the ship's side axis, z part)

503C.name: u1_cz
503C.desc: MS_CZ+M_U1: unit vector C,Z of the ship 1 download block, word (the ship's up axis, z part)

5042.name: u1_ty
5042.desc: MS_TY+M_U1: universe y position in the ship 1 download block, word, a copy of the ship's

5044.name: u1_tz
5044.desc: MS_TZ+M_U1: universe z position (height) in the ship 1 download block, word, a copy of the ship's

5080.name: s1_ax
5080.desc: MS_AX+M_S1: unit vector A,X of the player's ship, word: the x part of its forward axis, plus when the ship heads towards +x

5082.name: s1_ay
5082.desc: MS_AY+M_S1: unit vector A,Y of the player's ship, word: the x part of its side axis

5086.name: s1_vx
5086.desc: MS_VX+M_S1: the player's x speed, word

5088.name: s1_bx
5088.desc: MS_BX+M_S1: unit vector B,X of the player's ship, word: the y part of its forward axis

508E.name: s1_vy
508E.desc: MS_VY+M_S1: the player's y speed, word

5096.name: s1_vz
5096.desc: MS_VZ+M_S1: the player's z speed, word

509A.name: s1_ty
509A.desc: MS_TY+M_S1: the player's universe y position, word

509C.name: s1_tz
509C.desc: MS_TZ+M_S1: the player's universe z position (height), word

questions: B0:799F, B0:7A6B and elsewhere: the alias GM_WAV = $508A looks like a false match. $508A is unit vector B,Y of the player's ship block (MS_BY+M_S1): L6BC0 stores $C0 in $5080 and in it exactly as PHISG2 does with MS_AX+M_S1 and MS_BY+M_S1 (FACE BACKWARDS), and the movement code multiplies it by the sight deflection. Star Wars has GM_WAV at $4B15

names carried from Star Wars that no longer fit, left as they are: IPARM (B0:A39D) is the view routine of the probot wave and is identical, call for call, to VEWHPA (B0:A3DC), which views the phase that ends that wave. VEWG0D (B0:A41B) is the view of dying in the probot wave (called from L72F6 after PHIS0D), VEWGD (B0:A4E8) the view of dying in the walker wave (called from PHEG0D), VEWG1B (B0:A711) a death view with score, shields, the pseudo ROM picture and GAME OVER only (called from L740E). SMVG0B/SMVG9B (B0:7A2F) are the player movement of the walker wave, the same code as L7963, and S1MVBS (B0:78D0) is the player movement of the asteroid wave. The upper-case comments carried into the view routines are shifted against the calls they stand beside
B0:A729 VEWHPB: no call to it found in bank 0 or the slapstic pages - dead, or reached through a table I did not find

B0:7DD2-7DD9 (02 BB 5A 30 5F EE 05 A8): eight bytes after the two the self test reads at L7DD0/L7DD1, read by no code I found. Likewise B0:A316-A31B (04 BC 96 FA 5B 28) overwrite the first six letters of a plain ASCII line that otherwise reads '...ALLY MANAGED THE TEAM' (the carried comment gives Star Wars' text). Whether these are checksum or signature bytes I cannot tell from the code

B0:7DD0 and B0:A000: the self test shows the xor of one byte pair from each ROM when there are no errors. I describe them only as that - whether they are also what brings each ROM's checksum to the wanted value is not shown by the code
B0:7FFF: the last byte $96 after the complemented ' AGAIN' is not text (its complement is $69) - purpose unknown

B0:A763: I could not tell what the seven-piece picture at vector ROM $34A2-$3646 shows (colours 1 and 4, drawn receding to the upper right at the end of the asteroid wave), nor what the object of VWDTHB/LA8F8/LA843/LA881 (JSRL $298E in the pseudo ROM) is in ESB
B0:A342: the fourth entry of the set pointer table at LB97A is labelled DOXMT in the listing, which looks like a mislabelled data address (set 3)

B0:7CE6: Atari's name for the tic table is TRHTIC and belongs to $7CE3, inside the JSR at L7CE2 (the listing shows L7CE2+1) - entry 0 is never read. I labelled the first real entry tic_sin_cos instead of reusing the name
